## Solution

**Substitution.** Let $t = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, so that $\sqrt{n} = \dfrac{1}{t}$ and $t \to 0^{+}$ as $n \to \infty$. The expression becomes

$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\int_{1/\sqrt{n}}^{1}\frac{\ln(1+x)}{x^{3}}\,dx \;=\; t\int_{t}^{1}\frac{\ln(1+x)}{x^{3}}\,dx.$$

We seek $L = \displaystyle\lim_{t\to 0^{+}} t\int_{t}^{1}\frac{\ln(1+x)}{x^{3}}\,dx$.

**Isolating the singularity.** Write

$$\frac{\ln(1+x)}{x^{3}} \;=\; \frac{1}{x^{2}} \;+\; g(x), \qquad g(x) := \frac{\ln(1+x)-x}{x^{3}}.$$

Then

$$t\int_{t}^{1}\frac{\ln(1+x)}{x^{3}}\,dx \;=\; t\int_{t}^{1}\frac{dx}{x^{2}} \;+\; t\int_{t}^{1} g(x)\,dx \;=\; (1-t) \;+\; t\int_{t}^{1} g(x)\,dx.$$

**Bounding the remainder.** For $x \in [0,1]$, the Taylor expansion $\ln(1+x) = x - \tfrac{x^{2}}{2} + \tfrac{x^{3}}{3} - \cdots$ is alternating with decreasing terms, so

$$|\ln(1+x) - x| \;\le\; \frac{x^{2}}{2}, \qquad x \in [0,1].$$

Hence

$$|g(x)| \;=\; \frac{|\ln(1+x)-x|}{x^{3}} \;\le\; \frac{1}{2x}, \qquad x \in (0,1].$$

Therefore

$$\left|\,t\int_{t}^{1} g(x)\,dx\,\right| \;\le\; t\int_{t}^{1}\frac{dx}{2x} \;=\; \frac{t}{2}\ln\!\frac{1}{t} \;\xrightarrow[t\to 0^{+}]{}\; 0,$$

since $t\ln(1/t) \to 0$.

**Conclusion.**

$$L \;=\; \lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\bigl(1 - t\bigr) \;+\; \lim_{t\to 0^{+}} t\int_{t}^{1} g(x)\,dx \;=\; 1 + 0 \;=\; 1.$$

$$\boxed{\,1\,}$$
